title: U/L/R and repeat
author: Miller
desc:
Purely hypertrophy, but it's always possible to turn this into strength by lowering the rep count and going as heavy and explosive as possible. Volume in the sweet spot, but you have to have time and dedication to do these long sessions.


3 mins rest between each (super)set, no question about it. Can be more, but not below 3 mins.


Upper day will take around 2 hours.
Lower day can be done in 1.5 hours or even less if you time everything correctly.


Understand superset:
For example: lateral raise and shrugs superset -> do the first set of lateral raises and then take a 10 sec max breather and do the first set of shrugs. Rest 3 mins and repeat.


In the muscle activation preview, the middle delt might seem to be low rated, but since it's the very first exercise of the day, it will be one of the best developed since you're the freshest then, so make sure to go all the way to absolute failure on each set.


When systemic (CNS) fatigue kicks in, take 2 days off (upper and lower day). If you don't want to take those days off, then lower the usual weight by 50% and do not go to failure - @7 intensity.


Only use straps on deadlift. Nothing else. Not even a belt. This program is not limited to 12 weeks. It covers everything.

ex.note: Take the seat low, so that the upper back gets targeted more than the middle back.
One week concentration curls and one week incline curls. Keep switching each week.
1st set is warmup at 50% weight. 2nd set is at 80% weight. 3rd and 4th sets are at 100% weight for 4-6 reps. 3rd set is @9 intensity because of less accumulated fatigue.

ss.note: Use the same leg press machine to do your calf raises, but make sure to lock your knees, so that it simulates standing calf raises.
